We're looking for stories that centre Indigenous voices and leadership in innovation, where technology serves community sovereignty rather than replacing it.
_podcast.theme_scoring_prompt:
Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Indigenous Lands & Innovation' — Indigenous nations using technology, governance, and stewardship on their own terms.

OUT OF SCOPE — score 0-9: geopolitical and war news with no Indigenous rights angle; general wildfire and wildlife-service updates not led by or directly affecting Indigenous communities or guardians; provincial forestry and environmental policy with no explicit First Nations involvement; consumer tech and gadget reviews; science with no Indigenous stewardship or sovereignty context; crime and judicial news unrelated to Indigenous rights.

CALIBRATION — apply this ladder to everything else. Indigenous-led journalism on governance, rights, and self-determination is a strong fit on its own: a technology hook raises a score but is NOT required to reach the top band.
- 80-100: Excellent Indigenous-led reporting. Cariboo stories bridging governance or culture AND technology land here (Tŝilhqot'in/Secwépemc/Dakelh language revitalization tech, guardian programs using sensors and drones, GIS land mapping, Indigenous-led connectivity, digital heritage projects) — and so does outstanding national coverage of sovereignty, treaty, and land rights.
- 55-79: Solid pan-Canadian Indigenous governance, sovereignty, land rights, treaty, or reconciliation journalism — APTN, Eagle Feather News, or IndigiNews-style coverage of First Nations governance, MMIWG, land claims, self-determination, and Indigenous-led services. Most Indigenous governance journalism belongs HERE, not below.
- 30-54: Indigenous cultural, community, or human-interest stories (awards, events, ceremonies) with limited governance substance, or BC land-stewardship and environmental stories with meaningful First Nations involvement.
- 10-29: General BC land, environmental, or forestry stories that mention Indigenous communities only in passing.

ANCHORS: 'Tŝilhqot'in Nation launches drone-based caribou monitoring on title lands' → 98. 'First Nations leaders reject BC's revised land-title framework' → 75. 'Secwépemc language app reaches 1,000 learners' → 88. 'BC Wildfire Service updates evacuation alerts for the Interior' → 8.

Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

items.title: [livescience.com] Swallowable paper battery powers medical devices in pigs
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

Researchers developed a small battery made from magnesium and molybdenum trioxide that can be swallowed to power temporary medical devices inside the gastrointestinal tract. In pig tests, the battery produced a peak voltage of 1.84 volts and operated for up to three days, powering a wireless throat tag that transmitted to a receiver 1.5 metres away and a capsule that electrically stimulated the stomach for 20 minutes [scimex.org#1][livescience.com#1]. The battery uses materials intended to break down in the body after use, potentially removing the need to retrieve conventional batteries from temporary ingestible devices. The study remains at an early animal-testing stage: researchers tested a small number of pigs, and the circuit board did not fully degrade but passed in the animals' feces [scimex.org#1]. MIT said the researchers built two versions—a 7.5-millimetre disc and a 24-millimetre rectangular bar—for possible drug-delivery, sensing and other applications [mit.edu#1].

items.title: [ScienceDaily] James Webb reveals Chariklo’s mysterious rings are changing faster than expected
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

The James Webb Space Telescope has revealed surprising changes in the rings around Chariklo, a small object orbiting between Saturn and Uranus. Over just a few years, its inner ring became more opaque while its outer ring became less opaque. The results suggest that rings around small Solar System bodies may be much more dynamic than scientists previously believed. What is causing the changes remains a mystery.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Beyond the Replica: Digital Heritage and the Limits of Preservation
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

A cave in Maharashtra can now be entered without travelling to it. Through a virtual reality experience developed around Ajanta, visitors can move through a digitally reconstructed version of the caves from somewhere else entirely. The project raises an architectural question: if architecture is experienced through movement, scale, sequence and perception, what happens when those experiences can be recreated outside the physical site? IITM Pravartak's Digital Ajanta project uses 3D scanning, filming, modelling and virtual reality to document the caves and translate that record into an immersive experience.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] As president of Botswana, I know how we can make malaria a memory in Africa | Duma Gideon Boko
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

The disease is soaring as funding is cut. African nations are plugging the gap but they need help with the transition

Botswana nearly defeated malaria. In 2024, we recorded just 290 cases and one death. Through our elimination efforts, many of our districts had seen no local malaria cases since 2010. Then, as is unfortunately the nature of malaria, it came back.

In the first 23 weeks of 2025 we recorded 2,223 cases and 11 deaths. The disease reached places where previously there was no malaria. We were not alone. Namibia recorded more than 95,000 cases in 2025, and Zimbabwe more than 156,000, according to government figures.
